_comment: Correction-note evidence (S2): Llama-2-7B YaRN at the paper's actual
factors, measured twice so the anchor's contribution is separable.
For each (factor, context) the pair is mis-anchored vs correctly anchored.
The gate script writes the numbers (perplexity after a full-length prompt,
the generation's early-EOS/blank-line/repetition scores, and the effective
inv_freq it asserted from the built model). These are the evidence for the
correction note; they are NEVER reported as speculative-decoding results.
`expect` is deliberately absent: this is a measurement, and the gate's
pass/fail rule is not the point here. The claim under test is that the
anchor explains most of the perplexity damage and NOT the degeneration,
which is read off the numbers rather than off a verdict.

A DECLARED BASELINE IS REQUIRED. The gate computes each candidate's ratio against a row flagged `native_baseline`, at the candidate's own context; without one it refuses to write any numbers, so these two native rows are part of the evidence rather than decoration. A mis-anchored row with no baseline is not a measurement of damage -- it is a row nobody can interpret.

candidates.name: B_llama2_native_32k
candidates._what_it_is: Native Llama-2-7B at 32k: the reference the 32k rows are scored against. WITHOUT a declared baseline the gate refuses the whole stage ('no candidate is flagged native_baseline=true'), so the stage would spend a GPU window and produce no numbers at all.

candidates.name: B_llama2_native_128k
candidates._what_it_is: Native Llama-2-7B at 128k: the same role at the other context.
